restrictions: Two distinct 128-byte messages m(a), m(b) with equal complete 256-bit SHA3-256-r6 digests (an ordinary collision), encoded by the injective map u -> m(u) of proof.md Section 2: the four 64-bit limbs of u are placed in column x = 1 (lanes 1, 11, 6) and column x = 4 (lanes 9, 14, 4), and the other 10 lanes of the absorbed block hold the constants K_l of trial 27 of the 32-element annihilating linear-structure family (proof.md Section 2, from 7d11f600), so that round 0 is affine in u and annihilates 14 of the 25 lanes after round-0 chi; the search itself uses no algebraic property (F is only evaluated).
Complete SHA3-256 sponge of sha3-256-r6-prefix-v1: zero initial state, rate 136 bytes, suffix 0x06 with pad10*1, rounds 0 to 5 of Keccak-f[1600] in the single permutation call, full 256-bit digest.

Classical 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5 with reference operation cost 1626, a declared register file of 2,192 registers (H_reg, proof.md Section 3.5) and a 5-byte encoding of the straight-line step instructions alongside the assembled 32-byte non-straight-line machine code (H_code, proof.md Section 3.5 and Appendix D, following 18d9298d). One step of 256 walks costs BSTEP = 26,387 word operations (26,367 straight-line XOR/AND/OR/NOT operations with 1,213 10-gate chi rows, 15 prefilter ORs, 2 test and 3 counter operations); N = Tb * 26387 + replay + R + PRE = 35199200384660742826468319546036182727278 word operations (proof.md Section 4.4 and Appendix A), certified by 1626^100000 * 2^12402555 < N^100000 <= 1626^100000 * 2^12402556.

Memory at most 1,044,294 bytes <= 2^20 = 1,048,576 (margin 4,282 bytes; search phase 1,044,294 bytes with S = 23,088 table words of four 64-bit records each, preprocessing phase 869,115 bytes bound and 573,440 bytes measured resident peak, non-overlapping; memory_log2_bytes = 20, proof.md Section 6). Preprocessing is one run of the C generator `gen 32` (32 trial builds and one rebuild of trial 27, charged PRE = 33 * 2^32 + 32 * 2^10 = 141,733,953,536 word operations inside N; preprocessing_log2 = 27, proof.md Section 3.6). No advice.

No full-scale 2^124 run is executed. Correctness of the 26,367-operation straight-line step and the 2,704-instruction non-straight-line code is verified by execution against independent 6-round SHA3-256 implementations (`selftest.c`, `other4_test.py`, and `experiments/ls1.py`), and the score-critical random-function premise H_rand is tested by the organizer-executed experiments `rho-w22` and `proj-w256` and by the 2^24-evaluation C coincidence and differential suites (`hrand_test.c` and `proj_test.c`, proof.md Section 7).

heuristics.statement: Over the algorithm's random starting word rho, one attempt of the search of proof.md Section 4 run on the fixed SHA3-256-r6 chain function F(u) = SHA3-256-r6(m(u)) xor PD succeeds with probability at least the bound computed in proof.md Section 5 for a uniformly random function F: {0,1}^256 -> {0,1}^256, namely at least 0.3900000006 >= 0.39 at Tb = 535,677,142 * 2^91 steps of 256 walks (with distinguished-point threshold x < 704 * 2^135, theta = 704 * 2^-121, replay cap LRC = 62,557 * 2^99, table capacity U = 92,352 trails in S = 23,088 words of four records, and failure terms F6 = 3.153e-4, F2 = 3.703e-12, F3 = 1.137e-5, F4 = 6.060e-5, F5 < 2^-1000).
heuristics.scope: The transfer of the success probability lower bound of proof.md Section 5 from a uniformly random function M to the fixed deterministic 6-round chain function F(u) over the uniform random coin rho in {0,1}^256. Everything inside the random-function model M (the stopping-time coincidence distribution G(e), the bin sum over trail tail lengths, and the failure bounds F6, F2, F3, F4, F5) is proved in Section 5 and checked in 80-digit decimal and exact rational arithmetic in Appendix A.
heuristics.extrapolation: Tested by: (1) Organizer-executed experiment `rho-w22` (`experiments/ls1.py`), which runs the full Section 4 search (uncut trails, rational DP threshold theta = 5/128, replay length measurement and cap LRC = 256) on the 22-bit truncation of the exact 26,367-instruction straight line; across 2,304 trials (9 batches of 256), 2,304/2,304 return verified 22-bit collisions with mean 20.73 steps vs 20.47 for an ideal random function (z = +1.6). (2) Organizer-executed experiment `proj-w256` (`experiments/ls1.py`) and C `proj_test.c` at scale, running 8 chained full-width steps from 256 uniform starts per trial and checking for a 22-bit digest collision: 916/2,304 = 0.3976 (z = +0.4) in Python and 103,022/262,144 = 0.3930 (model 0.3934, z = -0.39) in C. (3) `hrand_test.c` on M = 2^24 full-width evaluations of `prog.bin` across three 32-bit windows (low, mid, top) for uniform inputs, consecutive inputs rho + i, and 256 chains of 65,536 iterates (all |z| <= 1.36), plus all 65,536 single-bit input/output difference cells (4,096 pairs each, max |z| = 4.59, mean z^2 = 1.0112). A pair-coincidence shortfall of 1 - eps relative to uniform shifts time_log2 by about 0.5 log2(1/(1 - eps)) bits (0.0073 bit for eps = 0.01).
heuristics.limitations: F is a fixed deterministic 6-round function whose first round is affine by construction of m(u), leaving 5 nonlinear rounds. Empirical tests check 22-bit and 32-bit projections up to 2^24 evaluations and reduced-width end-to-end searches at width 22..32, not the 256-bit coincidence rate over 2^128 evaluations.

heuristics.statement: The 256-bit word RAM of collision-frontier-v5 has a declared register file of 2,192 256-bit registers (70,144 bytes, charged in search memory in proof.md Section 6), so the 26,367-instruction straight-line step (which uses registers 0..2,180 with at most 1,925 simultaneously live values, while search state uses registers 2,181..2,190) executes register-to-register with 0 loads and 0 stores.
heuristics.scope: The register-file size and register-to-register operation charging of the straight-line step program in Section 3.5 and Section 6 (the same convention as 67f781f8, bc3e3eef, 7d11f600 and 18d9298d).
heuristics.extrapolation: Priced by `spill.py` (proof.md Section 8 and Appendix C) on the identical 26,367-instruction `prog.bin` under Belady furthest-next-use eviction when the register file is restricted: 1,024 registers adds 9,708 loads+stores per step (score 124.475, +0.45), 512 registers adds 15,520 (score 124.690, +0.66), 256 registers adds 20,347 (score 124.847, +0.82), and 64 registers adds 26,130 (score 125.014, +0.99).
heuristics.limitations: collision-frontier-v5 does not specify a fixed register file count; if fewer than 1,925 registers are available without memory traffic, register spills increase the step count as priced in Section 8.

heuristics.statement: Each register-only straight-line instruction (4 opcodes XOR/AND/OR/NOT and three 12-bit register indices) is encoded in 5 bytes (39 bits in little-endian order, 131,910 bytes for the 26,382 straight-line and prefilter instructions), while all 2,704 non-straight-line instructions are encoded in 32 bytes each (86,528 bytes, measured from `other.bin`), and each executed instruction is charged as the word operation(s) it performs with no separate instruction-fetch charge.
heuristics.scope: Code-memory footprint charging in proof.md Section 3.5 and Section 6 (following 67f781f8, bc3e3eef, 7d11f600 and 18d9298d).
heuristics.extrapolation: The 5-byte straight-line encoding and 32-byte non-straight-line encoding are decoded and executed directly by `selftest.c`, `hrand_test.c`, `proj_test.c`, and `other4_test.py` (Appendices B, C, D). Charging the straight line at 32 bytes per instruction instead of 5 bytes pushes code memory above 2^20 bytes and gives a score of about 124.71 (proof.md Section 8).
heuristics.limitations: collision-frontier-v5 does not specify a binary instruction width; charging 32 bytes per straight-line instruction instead of 5 bytes increases the code footprint by 712,314 bytes and raises the score to about 124.71.
